verses.1: Therefore, leaving behind the elementary teachings of the Messiah, let us press on toward maturity, not laying again a foundation of repentance from dead works, and of faith toward God,
verses.2: instruction on baptisms, the laying on of hands, resurrection of the dead, and eternal judgment.
verses.3: And we will do this, if God permits.
verses.4: For it is impossible for those who have once been enlightened, who have tasted the heavenly gift and have shared in the Holy Spirit,
verses.5: and have tasted the goodness of the word of God and the powers of the coming age,
verses.6: and have fallen away, to be brought back to repentance, for they crucify again for themselves the Son of God and put him to open shame.
verses.7: For the earth that drinks the rain that often comes on it and produces vegetation useful to those for whom it is farmed receives a blessing from God.
verses.8: But the one that bears thorns and thistles is worthless and near being cursed, whose end is to be burned.
verses.9: But we are confident about you, beloved, regarding better things, and things that accompany salvation, even as we speak thus:
verses.10: for God is not unjust to forget your work and the love that you showed for his name, as you have served the holy ones and still serve.
verses.11: And we desire that each one of you show the same eagerness to reach the fullness of your hope until the end,
verses.12: so that you do not become lazy, but imitate those who through faith and endurance inherit the promises.
verses.13: For when God made a promise to Abraham, because he had no one greater by whom to swear, he swore by himself,
verses.14: saying, "I will surely bless you, and I will surely multiply you."
verses.15: And so, having waited patiently, he obtained the promise.
verses.16: For people indeed swear by someone greater, and in every dispute an oath is the final confirmation, because it puts an end to all argument.
verses.17: In this way, God, desiring to show more abundantly to the heirs of the promise the immutability of his purpose, confirmed it with an oath,
verses.18: so that through two immutable things, in which it is impossible for God to lie, we may have strong encouragement to hold fast to the hope that is set before us,
verses.19: which we have like an anchor for the soul, sure and steadfast, and entering into the inner sanctuary behind the curtain,
verses.20: where Jesus, having gone as a forerunner for us, became a priest forever according to the order of Melchizedek.

notes:
Notes
- v. 6: "put him to open shame" (παραδειγματίζοντας) — the word is rare and can mean "exhibit as an example" or "publicly disgrace," both of which are consistent with the context. Chosen "open shame" for clarity and force.
- v. 18: "hold fast to the hope that is set before us" — "προκειμένης ἐλπίδος" is literally "the hope set before," but "set before us" is implied by context and is natural in English.
- v. 19: "entering into the inner sanctuary behind the curtain" — "ἐισερχομένην εἰς τὸ ἐσώτερον τοῦ καταπετάσματος" is a metaphorical reference to Christ's entrance into the heavenly sanctuary, not the earthly temple. Rendered accordingly.

[1] Therefore, leaving behind the elementary teachings of the Messiah, let us press on toward maturity, not laying again a foundation of repentance from dead works, and of faith toward God,
[2] instruction on baptisms, the laying on of hands, resurrection of the dead, and eternal judgment.
[3] And we will do this, if God permits.
[4] For it is impossible for those who have once been enlightened, who have tasted the heavenly gift and have shared in the Holy Spirit,
[5] and have tasted the goodness of the word of God and the powers of the coming age,
[6] and have fallen away, to be brought back to repentance, for they crucify again for themselves the Son of God and put him to open shame.
[7] For the earth that drinks the rain that often comes on it and produces vegetation useful to those for whom it is farmed receives a blessing from God.
[8] But the one that bears thorns and thistles is worthless and near being cursed, whose end is to be burned.
[9] But we are confident about you, beloved, regarding better things, and things that accompany salvation, even as we speak thus:
[10] for God is not unjust to forget your work and the love that you showed for his name, as you have served the holy ones and still serve.
[11] And we desire that each one of you show the same eagerness to reach the fullness of your hope until the end,
[12] so that you do not become lazy, but imitate those who through faith and endurance inherit the promises.
[13] For when God made a promise to Abraham, because he had no one greater by whom to swear, he swore by himself,
[14] saying, "I will surely bless you, and I will surely multiply you."
[15] And so, having waited patiently, he obtained the promise.
[16] For people indeed swear by someone greater, and in every dispute an oath is the final confirmation, because it puts an end to all argument.
[17] In this way, God, desiring to show more abundantly to the heirs of the promise the immutability of his purpose, confirmed it with an oath,
[18] so that through two immutable things, in which it is impossible for God to lie, we may have strong encouragement to hold fast to the hope that is set before us,
[19] which we have like an anchor for the soul, sure and steadfast, and entering into the inner sanctuary behind the curtain,
[20] where Jesus, having gone as a forerunner for us, became a priest forever according to the order of Melchizedek.

- v. 6: "put him to open shame" (παραδειγματίζοντας) — the word is rare and can mean "exhibit as an example" or "publicly disgrace," both of which are consistent with the context. Chosen "open shame" for clarity and force.
